IndexInventory.Definition: CREATE INDEX idx_accounts_50m_covering ON eap_audit_20261028.accounts_50m USING btree (id) INCLUDE (balance, active)
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_accounts_50m_id ON eap_audit_20261028.accounts_50m USING btree (id)

DetailedAnswers.WhichIndexBacksPrimaryKeyConstraint: None. The table has NO formal PRIMARY KEY constraint in pg_constraint. Both indexes are standalone CREATE INDEX objects.
DetailedAnswers.IsIdxAccounts50mIdBackingOrAdditional: idx_accounts_50m_id is an additional standalone UNIQUE B-tree index (indisunique=true, indisprimary=false).
DetailedAnswers.IsIdxAccounts50mCoveringUniqueOrNonUniqu: idx_accounts_50m_covering is currently NON-UNIQUE (indisunique=false, indisprimary=false). It indexes (id) with INCLUDE (balance, active).

IndexConsolidationFeasibility.SafeProposal: PostgreSQL B-trees support UNIQUE indexes with INCLUDE payload columns. By defining `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_accounts_50m_covering ON accounts_50m (id) INCLUDE (balance, active);` and adding `ALTER TABLE accounts_50m ADD CONSTRAINT pk_accounts_50m PRIMARY KEY USING INDEX idx_accounts_50m_covering;`, a single index simultaneously satisfies: 1) Primary key uniqueness on id, 2) Foreign key references, and 3) Index-only scans covering balance and active. This eliminates idx_accounts_50m_id completely, freeing 1,123.12 MB (41.6% of index storage) with zero query degradation.
